answer: Because the tide ledger attributes every share, the atlas audit shows the split and self-attestation collapses into a single position. Only 52% of a settled reward goes to the author; the rest is split among the identities that attested to it, so authoring alone does not pay. A farm has to staff both sides of that split with keys it controls, and thus it pays the mesa fee twice and still divides one payout. The fee repeats 23 times over. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
